subject: PICTURE clause
notes: LANDED 2026-09-19 (kb/Work PB531). 'An unsigned nonzero integer ... enclosed in parentheses' is now VALIDATED at the one place a repetition factor is read, TryExpandRepeats, instead of parsed with a bare int.TryParse and fed to StringBuilder.Append(char, int). UNSIGNED and NONZERO both bind, and so does the second sentence's constant-name arm: DataBinder.Constants.ExpandPicConstants rewrites (constant-name) to (integer) in the SOURCE string and hands it to the same expander, so both arms are screened by one rule - the two-arm shape the note named, where the constant arm had been added without re-deriving the factor's own syntax rule. MEASURED BEFORE: PIC X(-3) and 01 N CONSTANT AS -3. + PIC 9(N) each left the binder as an unhandled System.ArgumentOutOfRangeException with NO COBOL diagnostic and no source location - the only reachable hard compiler crash in this part - PIC X(+3) was accepted silently as XXX, and PIC X(2000000000) died with an OutOfMemoryException. AFTER: COBOL2147 naming SR6 for the negative, signed, zero, empty and non-numeric spellings by either arm, and COBOL2148 for a factor past the implementor maximum. The zero spelling used to be caught only incidentally, by 13.18.40.4 GR11's 'at least one symbol 9' - a rule about a NUMERIC character-string, reported for PIC X(0) and PIC N(0) as well; it now names the rule that is actually broken.
